title: Working Virginia's nights and the union days
summary: Howard describes holding two jobs, playing till 2 a.m. and being at the union by 10.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: And actually, when you were working
in Virginia you were actually being secretary of the union. Financial secretary of the union.
Yeah.
You had like a double job going for all those years.
I did. I had a double job going.
When did you sleep?
Didn't sleep.
So what time would you get home, for example? Virginia's closed about 2:00?
2:00, yeah. It closed at 2:00 o'clock and I'd get home about three.
Did you still live where you're living now?
Right here.
Okay. Now, you didn't have the --
I've been married to Susie a long time.
Yeah. You didn't have the freeways like you have now, did you?
No.
So what time would you get home, 3:30, 4:00 in the morning?
About 3:00.
And what time did you have to be. --
-- at the union, at what, 10:00 in the morning?
Huh?
What time did you have to be at the union the next day?
Oh, about 10:00 in the morning.
So you got about four hours, five hours rest.
Yeah, you know what I did? I was thinking about that this morning, and I said, "Gee, I wonder if I'll be able to tell Buddy all these things when he comes back again next time."
Thinking about what, working in the night and the day?
Yeah.
It's important to know the kind of guy you were. You were doing great work on two ends there. You were top man in the daytime at the union and --
